description: Hand-built cases for the IFEval startend:quotation (QuotationChecker) audit. Each text is given as Unicode code points so this file is pure ASCII. 'shipped' = IFEval's reading (stripped value starts and ends with the ASCII QUOTATION MARK U+0022); 'intended' = stripped value starts and ends with a double quotation mark of any script (Unicode name contains QUOTATION MARK and DOUBLE, or is U+0022; single quotes excluded). A flip means the shipped checker and the intended reading disagree on whether the response is wrapped in double quotation marks.

cases.note: LEFT/RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK U+201C..U+201D wrapping 'hello'. These curly typographic quotes are emitted by many models, editors and markdown renderers. The response is plainly wrapped in double quotes, yet shipped sees no ASCII U+0022 -> FAIL (a false fail).
DOUBLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK U+201E open and LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK U+201C close (German style). Both are double quotation marks; shipped FAIL, intended PASS.
LEFT/RIGHT-POINTING DOUBLE ANGLE QUOTATION MARK U+00AB..U+00BB (French/German double quotes). Unicode names them double angle quotation marks; shipped FAIL, intended PASS.
Control: plain ASCII QUOTATION MARK U+0022 at both ends. Both the shipped and intended readings see the response as wrapped -> PASS, no flip.
Control: no quotation marks at all. Both readings see no wrapping -> FAIL, no flip.

LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK U+201C open, ASCII QUOTATION MARK U+0022 close -- a frequent artefact when an opening smart quote is auto-substituted but the closing one is not. Shipped sees the first char is not ASCII U+0022 -> FAIL; intended PASS. One non-ASCII boundary is enough to break the shipped check.
